$comment: Host tool propose_memory. On chat requests that can carry tools the model proposes long-term memories itself; the host turns each call into at most one pending candidate through memory-intent.v1 makeMemoryCandidate, after its own deterministic checks (arguments, the quote must come from this turn's user message, secret / special-category rejection). Nothing becomes an active memory item without the user accepting it. Paths that cannot carry tools fall back to the memory-intent.v1 deterministic route. Clients load `tool` and `toolResult` byte-for-byte; projections must equal what each client's production tool projection outputs for [tool]. Model behaviour itself is out of scope (measured by scripts/memory-intent-offline-gate.mjs). v2: kinds add decision / event (episodicKinds); a candidate's proposedLayer is episodic for those kinds and semantic otherwise.

function.name: propose_memory
function.description: Propose one long-term memory for the user to confirm. Call it only when the user's own message in this turn asks you to remember something for future conversations, or states a lasting fact or preference about themselves, or a decision or event they will want to look up later, that they clearly want kept beyond this conversation. One atomic statement per call, keeping the user's meaning and language; never record your own inference. Do not call it for: instructions such as 'from now on' or 'going forward' unless the user says they apply to all or future chats (those stay in this conversation); reminders and to-dos; questions, including 'can you remember...'; corrections or statements that something is no longer true; quoted, hypothetical or role-play text; anything containing passwords, keys, codes, payment or ID details, health, sexuality, religion, politics, ethnicity, criminal record or immigration status. Nothing is saved until the user confirms. After calling, continue your reply normally and do not mention the proposal.

algorithm: 1 Mode (per fresh chat send, decided before the request is built): none when purpose != chat or the send is not a fresh user send (retry, regenerate, edit, continue, recovery); fallback when effective useMemory is off, the local auto-suggest switch is off, the request cannot carry client tools (the same predicate that gates MCP tools: Free, Managed, image generation, non-tool transports, capability evidence unsupported, remembered tool-call false; plus a request that runs the Moonshot built-in $web_search loop, which rejects any other tool name) or the connection is degraded (rule 6); tool otherwise.

2 mode=tool: append `tool` as the last entry of the request tools (after MCP / library tools), tool_choice auto. The memory-intent.v1 memory route does not run for that message (no v1 memory candidate, no memory-off hint); the conversation-instruction bar still follows memory-intent.v1 classify. mode=fallback: exactly the memory-intent.v1 route as before (memory candidate, memory-off hint, conversation-instruction bar). mode=none: neither.

3 Execution: every propose_memory call in the turn is answered with `toolResult` byte-for-byte, whatever the outcome (invalid arguments included; never a ToolCallRejection, never an error payload), so the model never retries or asks about it. The call and its result are not shown as tool steps, are not persisted into the conversation history or step records, and are not sent again on later turns.

4 propose(arguments, context, priorInTurn), in order: priorInTurn >= maxProposalsPerTurn -> turn_limit (priorInTurn counts earlier propose_memory calls of the same turn, whatever their outcome). arguments must parse as a JSON object whose proposition and sourceQuote are strings, kind is in memory-intent.v1 kinds or episodicKinds and scope is in `scopes`, else invalid_arguments. content = proposition with White_Space trimmed (memory-intent trim); quote = memoryIntentCanonical(sourceQuote); content or quote empty -> invalid_arguments. content longer than memory-intent contentMaxCodePoints code points -> too_long. memoryIntentCanonical(context.userText) must contain quote, else quote_not_in_message (userText = the text of the fresh user message of this turn). sensitive(x) = memory-intent.v1 classify(x).sensitive: secret for userText, content or sourceQuote -> secret; special for content or sourceQuote -> special. memory-intent.v1 classify(userText) has suggestion = conversationInstruction or blocked = conversation_scope -> conversation_instruction (conversation-scoped rules belong to the conversation-instruction bar, never to memory). Otherwise return memory-intent.v1 makeMemoryCandidate for the classification {intent: implicit_persist, proposition: content, kind, scope, sensitive: none, blocked: null, suggestion: memory} and context {conversationId, folderId, messageId, nowMs, activeContents, records} with autoSuggest absent; so id = UUIDv5(messageId \n fingerprint) (the same message and proposition from both routes collide on id), confidence = memory-intent constants.confidence.implicit_persist, scope mapping per memory-intent candidateScope. The candidate's proposedLayer = episodic when kind is in episodicKinds, else semantic (memory-items memoryLayerOfKind); accepting a candidate creates the item in the layer of its final kind.

5 Suggestion bar: the first created candidate of the turn becomes the "save to memory?" bar under that turn's assistant reply, shown once the reply stops streaming; the other candidates stay in the inbox. The fallback route shows its bar under the assistant reply of the same turn too.

6 Degrade: when a request that carried `tool` is rejected and the rejection qualifies (tool-unsupported-4xx.json matcher true, first leg, before any stream output, no structured tool call seen) the client resends this turn once without tools (existing behaviour), runs the fallback route for this message, and marks connectionId \n model id as degraded in memory for the rest of the process. Existing tool-call memory writes stay as they are. HTTP 422 follows each client's existing matcher (Web excludes it, iOS / Android follow tool-unsupported-4xx.json) and is not locked here. A rejection after output, on a later leg, or judged model access denied is surfaced unchanged.

7 Tail leg (plain chat path, no MCP / library loop): the first leg streams as usual with `tool` attached. If it ends asking for tool results and every call it made is propose_memory, the host executes them (rule 4) and sends at most one tail leg: the same history plus the assistant tool-call message (carrying the first leg's provider continuation: reasoning_content, thinking signatures, previous_response_id) and one `toolResult` per call, tools still attached with tool_choice none. propose_memory calls inside the tail leg are executed but never trigger another leg. Replay state is only required when the first leg carried reasoning (reasoning_content, thinking signatures, stateful previous_response_id); without reasoning the tail leg uses the ordinary message shape on every protocol. If required replay state is missing: a non-empty first-leg text ends the turn; an empty one triggers one resend of the original request without tools. The delivered text is the first-leg text followed by the tail-leg text. Usage adds both legs; stopReason comes from the last leg; a first leg that ended on tool calls is not an empty answer and not an unhandled-tool card. Calls to any other tool name keep today's unhandled-tool behaviour. Inside the MCP / library loops propose_memory is one more registry entry (rule 2 order) and does not count as retrieval for first-leg-without-tool-call checks.
